title: Surge crediting and tokenized metering for oversubscribed KV warmups
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During short-lived traffic surges we observe repeated speculative KV warmups and prefix cache population that are amortized across many downstream microbatches. Current metering attributes full token cost to the first microbatch owner (or prorates awkwardly), which inflates a single tenant's billed usage and triggers quota enforcement in surprising ways. This ticket designs a pragmatic alternative: 'surge crediting' plus 'tokenized metering'.

Goal: Avoid surprise billing/quota spikes for customers while preserving conservative rate-limit behavior and accounting integrity. We want deterministic, debuggable cost attribution for burst-driven KV warmups and prefix loads without materially increasing system complexity or latency.

Scope: Design and implement a server-side metering policy that: (1) identifies short-lived warmup events (heuristics based on origin, TTL, and collision window), (2) issues transient surge credits to early consumers, (3) attaches a reusable tokenized-meter record to the warmed entry that tracks provenance and amortized cost, and (4) adjusts quota deductions and rate-limit tokens according to tokenized amortization rules. This affects the runtime metering pipeline, quota enforcement path, billing export, and Console cost breakdown UI.

Out of scope: Full rework of global quota algorithms, cross-region reconciliation, or long-term accounting changes to invoices. This is a service-side metering change that keeps invoices unchanged except for corrected event-level attribution exported to billing pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Surge warmup detection correctly flags >90% of observed short-lived warmup events in staging without false-positives above 10% (measured on a 48h traffic replay)
When surge credits are applied, affected customers see a normalized per-request token count in Console and billing-export (no single microbatch >20% above expected baseline for the replay),
Quota enforcement still prevents abusive traffic: rate-limit windows and hard quota thresholds remain enforced and are visible in debug traces
Billing export contains provenance tag for tokenized-meter entries so downstream invoice pipelines can be reconciled if needed
E2E tests covering mixed-tenant coalesced warmup flows and a load test demonstrating <5% median latency regression for warmup path
design_notes: We will implement a lightweight warmup detector in the request router: mark a key as 'surge-warmup' when multiple unique tenants access same prefix within a 500ms collision window and backend KV entry age < 2s.
Surge credits are ephemeral: emit a credit record (credit ID token) tied to the warmed key that grants a fixed token discount to the next N microbatches (configurable, default N=8) or up to 10s.

Tokenized-metering model: instead of charging the first request full cost, we create a token record that contains an amortized token ledger; owners consume token segments on subsequent microbatches. The ledger is exported as a single provenance entry for reconciliation.

Quota semantics: credits do not bypass hard quotas; they adjust billed token amounts but rate-limit counters (requests/sec) remain unchanged. We add a secondary quota deduction pathway that consumes 'credit tokens' before debiting the tenant's primary quota bucket.

Trade-offs considered: (a) Full per-tenant proration vs token ledger — token ledger chosen for easier traceability and lower RPC chatter. (b) Conservative detection window reduces missed warmups but risks extra credits; we bias for false-negatives in early rollout.
Data model changes: add 'meter_token_id' and 'meter_provenance' fields to runtime usage events. These are flat string tags that map to the exported amortization record.
Console UX: expose 'surge credit' events in per-route cost breakdown, with an ability to toggle raw vs amortized view for debugging (PM to spec).
Backward compatibility: if downstream billing consumers ignore 'meter_token_id', behavior falls back to existing full-charge semantics.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gated implementation behind 'surge-crediting' and 'tokenized-metering' flags
2) Stage: deploy to internal-staging with synthetic traffic replay and 48h observation window
3) Canary: enable for 5% of hosted API traffic (non-enterprise) and monitor billing deltas and quota hits over 7 days
4) Expand: 25% -> 100% if metrics stable and no customer complaints; enable Console UX for internal users first
5) Post-rollout: run nightly reconciliation job for 7 days that compares tokenized exports to baseline billing to validate numeric invariants
metrics: % of warmup events detected (target > 90% on replay)
Median and 95th percentile per-request billed tokens for affected tenants (target: <=20% deviation from baseline after amortization)
Number of surprise quota hits attributed to warmups per day (target: 0 after rollout for test cohort)
Console 'raw vs amortized' usage view adoption and feedback
Additional CPU/latency on hot path (target: <5% median increase)
Volume of tokenized-meter provenance records emitted per hour
